P085: the prep parsers (mail-parser Apache-2.0 port, attribution header + notice mail_parser.json) were ported; URLs are unwrapped through the real P064 helper v3lum.modules.url_web.url_unwrap.unwrap_url (lazy import; without it wrapped URLs stay unwrapped and are never pivoted - no second implementation); recipients/reporters are redacted from every attribute/finding/pivot (shareable view) and kept only in res.raw['local_only'] (local case evidence); the main .eml fixture is synthetic in real header grammar (no real reported e-mail can be committed with its personal data), the malformed one is a scrubbed derivative of mail-parser's real spam sample. P088: Kickbox Open terms recorded as 'unknown' (no published terms for the free endpoint), MailCheck.ai/UserCheck as 'open' (free plan, no resale/redistribution of results: internal use) with its documented keyless budget (5/hour/IP) as the provider quota; Disify not used; no SMTP anywhere. P132: domain lookups answered locally from the 24 h catalogue dataset (?domain= never called; wording 'this service was breached - not accounts at this domain' in attributes and findings); /breach/{name} only for names unknown to the local copy; /latestbreach probes a stale copy before re-downloading 1.1 MB (HIBP sends no ETag), remembered 24 h in ctx.state; LogoPath, Attribution (holds people's handles/e-mails in the real catalogue) and DisclosureUrl are dropped by the hibp.catalog P145 schema before cache, dataset copy and evidence; sensitive breaches masked by default (setting hibp_catalog_show_sensitive); e-mail input deliberately not accepted (see backlog). V3LUM_HIBP_KEY and api.pwnedpasswords.com are not used (cond 1: keyless catalogue only). P134: allowlist schemas live in the hudsonrock provider fragment and are applied by the HTTP client before cache/module; the module rebuilds records from the same allowlist; urls-by-domain is fetched no-store and stripped in memory; 30 s per request; run_on own_assets (identity) and own_assets_only (domain) plus in-module scope checks (defence in depth); A4 BR13 end-to-end grep test over cache DB, evidence, case DB, html/md/json/stix reports, events and DEBUG logs.
